c.tagline: The 'Venice of the Alps,' where a canal-laced old town meets one of Europe's cleanest lakes

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small market stalls

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €3.50 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: The old town canal district is compact and very walkable; the lakeside promenade extends further and is best explored on foot or by bike

safety.safety: Very safe city with a relaxed, family-friendly atmosphere
safety.crime: Petty theft near the old town and lakefront in peak summer is the main concern

hood_landmark.Vieille Ville (Old Town): The Palais de l'Isle on the Thiou river
hood_landmark.Lakefront (Bord du Lac): The Pont des Amours and lakeside gardens
hood_landmark.Château Quarter: The Château d'Annecy museum on the hill above town
hood_landmark.Le Pâquier: Le Pâquier lakeside park and swimming area
hood_landmark.Vélo Bleu / Cycling Path (toward Talloir: The lakeside cycling path toward Talloires

avoid.reason: Watch for pickpockets in the crowded old-town lanes and lakefront during peak summer.

hood_desc: The canal-laced medieval core with the Palais de l'Isle and pastel-colored buildings; the natural base for any visit.
The lake's edge promenade with gardens, swimming spots, and the romantic Pont des Amours, a short walk from the old town.
A hilltop quarter above the old town with the historic château and sweeping views over the lake and mountains.
A popular lakeside park for swimming, picnics, and lounging, especially lively in summer.
The scenic lakeside cycling and walking path leading south toward Talloires and other lake villages, ideal for a longer active day out.

water.note: Tap water is safe and good quality throughout the city.

transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: The old town and lakefront are best explored on foot or bike; buses serve outlying neighborhoods

transport.air: Geneva Airport (GVA, Switzerland), about 45 min away; Lyon-Saint Exupéry (LYS) is a further alternative
transport.train: TGV and regional trains connect to Lyon, Geneva, and Paris
transport.bus: Regional buses connect to alpine villages and ski resorts
transport.ferry: Seasonal lake boat services connect Annecy to Talloires and other lakeside villages
transport.car: Well connected via the A41 motorway; the old town is pedestrian-friendly

airport.name: Geneva Airport (main regional gateway)
airport.transport: Train, shuttle bus, or rental car

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An Orange, SFR, or Bouygues tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for guides and tours
tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up is a nice gesture, not expected
